title: Why do stars have different colors?
challenge: Compare two explanations of stellar color and explain the relationship between temperature and light.

title: How does sleep reshape memory?
challenge: Find evidence for what the sleeping brain does with new memories and explain it without jargon.

title: Why do some diseases spread faster than others?
challenge: Identify three factors that affect disease spread and show how they interact.

title: What makes an ecosystem resilient?
challenge: Use one real ecosystem to explain how diversity and adaptation support recovery.

title: How do vaccines train the immune system?
challenge: Explain immune memory and compare how two vaccine types create protection.

title: Why do ocean currents shape climate?
challenge: Trace one major current and explain how it redistributes heat around the planet.

title: Can plants communicate with each other?
challenge: Compare chemical, fungal, and airborne signaling claims using evidence from plant research.

title: What causes the northern lights?
challenge: Follow energy from the Sun to the atmosphere and explain why auroras have different colors.

title: Why do antibiotics stop working?
challenge: Explain antibiotic resistance through natural selection and identify two ways to slow it.

title: How does the brain predict the world?
challenge: Investigate predictive processing and use one illusion to show how expectations affect perception.

title: What limits the human lifespan?
challenge: Compare two biological theories of ageing and assess what current evidence supports.

title: Could life exist beyond Earth?
challenge: Define the conditions scientists search for and evaluate one promising world beyond Earth.

title: Why does a chorus feel memorable?
challenge: Compare two memorable choruses and identify the musical patterns that help them stick.

title: How does rhythm change emotion?
challenge: Choose contrasting rhythms and explain how tempo, repetition, and syncopation affect feeling.

title: Why do some chords create tension?
challenge: Explain consonance and dissonance through one song or composition you know.

title: How has recording technology changed music?
challenge: Trace one recording innovation and show how it changed what musicians could create.

title: Why does bass change how music feels?
challenge: Compare the role of bass in two genres and explain its rhythmic and emotional effects.

title: What is perfect pitch?
challenge: Investigate how perfect pitch develops and whether training, language, or genetics matters most.

title: How does musical improvisation work?
challenge: Study one improvisational tradition and explain how knowledge and spontaneity work together.

title: Why do instruments have different voices?
challenge: Use harmonics and timbre to explain why the same note sounds different across instruments.

title: Why can music unlock old memories?
challenge: Explore how music connects memory, emotion, and personal identity in the brain.

title: How does silence function in music?
challenge: Analyze how pauses and silence create expectation in two contrasting compositions.

title: How do musical traditions evolve?
challenge: Trace how one musical tradition changed through migration, technology, or cultural exchange.

title: Has streaming changed the shape of songs?
challenge: Compare songs across eras and assess how streaming incentives affect length and structure.

title: Why do certain colors feel warm?
challenge: Compare cultural and perceptual explanations for warm and cool color associations.

title: How does negative space guide attention?
challenge: Analyze two artworks or designs where empty space changes what the viewer notices.

title: What makes an image feel balanced?
challenge: Compare symmetry and asymmetry in two images and explain why both can feel balanced.

title: Why do artistic styles repeat?
challenge: Choose one revived artistic style and investigate why it returned in a new era.

title: How does perspective create depth?
challenge: Compare linear perspective with another depth technique across two artworks.

title: Why does texture matter in art?
challenge: Study how real and implied texture change the experience of two works.

title: What can a portrait reveal about identity?
challenge: Compare two portraits and examine how pose, setting, and symbolism construct identity.

title: Why did artists turn to abstraction?
challenge: Investigate one abstract movement and the problem its artists were trying to solve.

title: How does public art change a city?
challenge: Evaluate one public artwork through the perspectives of artists, residents, and officials.

title: How does typography create mood?
challenge: Compare how type choices alter the tone and trustworthiness of the same message.

title: Can photography tell the truth?
challenge: Examine framing, selection, and editing in two photographs that claim to document reality.

title: How do museums shape the meaning of art?
challenge: Explore how labels, placement, and institutional history affect how one artwork is understood.

title: What makes an action morally right?
challenge: Apply two ethical frameworks to the same dilemma and compare their conclusions.

title: Can we know anything with certainty?
challenge: Compare skepticism with one response to it and state which argument you find stronger.

title: What gives a life meaning?
challenge: Compare two philosophical views of meaning and test them against an everyday life.

title: Are we the same person over time?
challenge: Explore memory, body, and continuity theories through one identity thought experiment.

title: Do we really have free will?
challenge: Compare determinism and compatibilism, then test both against an everyday decision.

title: Is fairness the same as equality?
challenge: Apply equality, equity, and need-based fairness to one real allocation problem.

title: What is consciousness?
challenge: Compare two theories of consciousness and identify what evidence could distinguish them.

title: Is beauty in the eye of the beholder?
challenge: Compare subjective and objective accounts of beauty using one disputed artwork.

title: What makes authority legitimate?
challenge: Compare consent, justice, and effectiveness as grounds for political authority.

title: What do we owe future generations?
challenge: Use climate or technology policy to compare duties to present and future people.

title: Can truth be relative?
challenge: Distinguish disagreement, perspective, and relativism through a concrete example.

title: Does technology help us live well?
challenge: Evaluate one everyday technology through two different ideas of the good life.

title: How do recommendation systems shape taste?
challenge: Map how one recommendation system learns from behavior and influences future choices.

title: Why does encryption protect privacy?
challenge: Explain public-key encryption with a simple analogy, then identify where the analogy breaks.

title: What makes an interface feel intuitive?
challenge: Compare two interfaces and identify the cues that reduce the amount users must remember.

title: How could AI change creative work?
challenge: Find evidence for one opportunity and one risk, then form your own position.

title: How does the internet find the right destination?
challenge: Trace a web request through names, addresses, routers, and servers.

title: Why do passwords keep failing us?
challenge: Compare passwords, password managers, passkeys, and multi-factor authentication.

title: How does blockchain create trust?
challenge: Explain consensus without jargon and identify where blockchain is—and is not—useful.

title: What makes software scale?
challenge: Study one high-traffic system and identify how it handles growth and failure.

title: How does data compression work?
challenge: Compare lossless and lossy compression using text, images, or sound.

title: Why does accessibility improve technology?
challenge: Trace one accessibility feature from a specific need to broader everyday usefulness.

title: Why does open-source software work?
challenge: Study one open-source project and explain how contribution, governance, and funding interact.

title: How will automation reshape work?
challenge: Compare historical automation with current AI adoption and identify what may be different.

title: Why do stories survive across generations?
challenge: Trace one enduring story and identify what changed—and what stayed stable—over time.

title: How do cities shape creativity?
challenge: Compare two cities and investigate how density, diversity, and institutions affect creative work.

title: Why do rituals strengthen communities?
challenge: Study one ritual and explain how repetition, symbols, and participation build belonging.

title: How does language shape thought?
challenge: Compare evidence for and against linguistic influence on perception or memory.

title: How does food carry identity?
challenge: Trace one dish across migration, memory, and changing ideas of authenticity.

title: What does fashion communicate?
challenge: Compare how one style signals belonging, status, resistance, or identity.

title: Why do cultures create myths?
challenge: Compare myths from two cultures and identify the problems each story helps people understand.

title: How does migration transform culture?
challenge: Follow one cultural practice across migration and examine what adapts, blends, or persists.

title: Why is humor different across cultures?
challenge: Compare what makes two cultures laugh and what gets lost when humor is translated.

title: Why do festivals endure?
challenge: Study one festival and explain how ritual, commerce, memory, and change coexist.

title: How do sports create belonging?
challenge: Explore how one team or sport builds identity through symbols, stories, and shared emotion.

title: What changes when ideas are translated?
challenge: Compare translations of one idea and examine what each version preserves or transforms.
